findings.source_passage: at any rate, it is pleasant to read about whales through their own spectacles, as you may say
findings.source_locator: paragraph 3, after description of isinglass substance
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves the line but drops the preceding whimsical build-up: 'I have sometimes pleased myself with fancying it exerted a magnifying influence' — the self-deprecating, digressive voice that makes the spectacles quip land. Without it the quip loses its comic scaffolding.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'I have sometimes pleased myself with fancying it exerted a magnifying influence' before the spectacles line to preserve the ironic, self-amused register.

findings.source_passage: creatures, that warm themselves under the lee of an iceberg, as a traveller in winter would bask before an inn fire
findings.why_it_matters: This simile is a characteristically Melvillean domestic-comic analogy (the inn-fire) that gives the cold-fish contrast its rhetorical colour; the draft collapses it to 'may bask under the lee of an iceberg,' losing the voice-establishing wit.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the inn-fire simile: 'creatures that warm themselves under the lee of an iceberg, as a traveller in winter would bask before an inn fire.'

findings.source_passage: where, when seamen fall overboard, they are sometimes found, months afterwards, perpendicularly frozen into the hearts of fields of ice
findings.why_it_matters: The draft drops 'perpendicularly' — a single word that makes the image grotesquely precise and memorable; its omission softens a characteristically stark Melville detail.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'perpendicularly frozen into the hearts of fields of ice' verbatim.

findings.source_passage: the rare virtue of a strong individual vitality, and the rare virtue of thick walls, and the rare virtue of interior spaciousness
findings.why_it_matters: The triple anaphora ('the rare virtue of … and the rare virtue of … and the rare virtue of') is the rhetorical engine that propels the sermon-like peroration; collapsing it to a list with commas and no anaphora strips the passage of its incantatory signature rhythm.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full tricolon: 'the rare virtue of a strong individual vitality, and the rare virtue of thick walls, and the rare virtue of interior spaciousness.'

summary: No high-severity signature losses; two medium-severity voice-flattenings (the magnifying-influence build-up and the inn-fire simile) and two low-severity rhythm/detail compressions are present, but the critical signatures — the hieroglyphics passage, the poncho image, the Borneo-negro line, and the St. Peter's peroration — are all preserved adequately.
